Consume a planner bundle (.bale-bundle; BALE.md §6.7) and pack its session,
cheapest gate first, every refusal landing before any session state exists.
(1) Gate bundle.json through validate_bundle_manifest before trusting anything
else, and verify each member's published sha256 against its LF-normalized
bytes. (2) Parse the stored pack argv with the real CLI parser and run the
arg-inspectable pack gates — forecast existence, then forecast disjointness,
the same implementations `bale pack` runs (board 68) — so a bundle the replay
would refuse on its argv alone refuses here, in that gate's own words, with no
dry-run spent; refusals name the resolved project root and the config files
judged. (3) When the bundle ships a checkpoint, refuse up front if the project
pins no [validation] base, then dry-run the checkpoint read-only against a
scratch copy of the live base and echo the expected-HOLD proof (exit 1
expected; exit 2 refuses the whole open as a defective oracle; exit 0 proceeds
with a vacuous-oracle warning). (4) Replay the stored pack argv with --readme-
file/--no-readme and --checkpoint-file injected from member presence and the
bundle's pre_answered intents riding the in-process channel — routed through
every decline-default exchange, never around it. The replayed pack re-runs
every gate at its own site; the early gates are a cost ordering, not a
substitute.
